rendered:
The document doesn't support this premise. It never gives a limit of detection for S. aureus, so it can't say why S. aureus would have the lowest. LODs are reported only for P. aeruginosa and L. monocytogenes: P. aeruginosa had an LOD of OD600 =0.0034 (CD,[1] (compared with 0.0066 (UV–vis, Fig. S17b)[2]), and L. monocytogenes[3], which presented an LOD of 0.0123 (CD, Fig. S17c) versus 0.0125 (UV–vis,[4]). Of this pair, P. aeruginosa has the lower LOD.

The data that do mention S. aureus suggest it was among the weakest-responding strains, not the most sensitive. In panel a of Fig. 2[5], the vision-model reading puts the CD difference for S. aureus at the bottom of the series, decreasing from P. aeruginosa to S. aureus.[6][7] In the concentration-gradient tests, S. aureus was only partly distinguished from the others: only partial discrimination was achieved for S. typhimurium and S. aureus (Fig. S18b-c)[8].

The paper's only general point about LOD is that CD consistently achieved lower limit of detection (LOD) than UV–vis.[9] If an S. aureus LOD exists, it would be in the Supplementary Information, which isn't part of this document.
